semantic_law.input: Finite ordered sequence of finite strings over {0,1}; empty word allowed, duplicate codewords retain their original indices.
semantic_law.output: CERTIFIED(p,q) with exact reduced dyadic Kraft sum p/q when no two distinct indexed words are prefix comparable; otherwise NOT_PREFIX_FREE(i,j,prefix) for lexicographically first index pair i<j with one word a prefix of the other, including equality.
semantic_law.failure: Nonbinary words, non-string elements, or non-finite/non-sequence input rejected explicitly; no silent coercion.
rules: The empty codeword is a valid complete code by itself (Kraft=1); two empty codewords conflict.
The empty list is certified with Kraft sum 0.
Kraft <=1 is necessary for actual prefix-free words, not sufficient for those already chosen words.
The first conflicting pair is ordered by input indices (i,j), not by word lexical ordering.
No physical SENS/T5/Framed3 code authority follows from a mathematical certificate.

source.primary_scope: MIT Coding for Discrete Sources §2.3.3, Kraft inequality for actual prefix-free codes; exact first-conflict witness is new SENS research interface, not an assertion of MIT API.

behavioral_neighbors: D2 frame parsing and Framed3 research
dedup.observation: Only this proposal couples explicit prefix-conflict witness on a concrete codebook to exact dyadic Kraft total; naming is not itself a proof of semantic irreducibility.
dedup.core_vs_library: PENDING OWNER REVIEW: certificate is mathematically composable from string-prefix comparisons and exact arithmetic.

independent_oracles: Pairwise all index pairs + rational Fraction summation.
Dyadic cylinder integer intervals on common depth + disjointness and integer volume.

checks.exhaustive: 3616 ordered collections of up to 3 words drawn from all binary words length 0..3; 8 positive/negative witnesses; 4 invalid-input reject cases
